attempts.summary: Configured node1 and node2 (SONiC switches) to learn each other's private downstream networks (node3's 192.168.10.0/24 and node4's 192.168.20.0/24) via iBGP over a direct transit link (172.20.1.0/31), instead of manually entered routes. node3 and node4 now reach each other purely through BGP-learned routes installed on node1/node2 (node3/node4 each keep only a normal static default-gateway route to their own local switch, which is standard host configuration, not a hand-entered route to the remote network). Configuration was made to survive reboot: FRR neighbor/network config is reapplied via a boot-time systemd unit (antrieb-bgp-apply.service) because SONiC's bgpcfgd regenerates bgpd.conf from configdb templates on every container start; BGP router-id persisted via the supported DEVICE_METADATA.bgp_router_id configdb field + config save; eth1/eth2 addressing persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d; forwarding sysctls persisted via /etc/sysctl.d; docker0's class-E IP stripped via a boot-time systemd unit (antrieb-netfix.service); node3/node4 static default-route-style entries persisted via systemd-networkd .network files. All four nodes were restarted one at a time (never concurrently, quorum/route symmetry preserved throughout), each showed a changed OS boot_id proving an actual reboot, and after each restart the required services (SONiC docker containers, BGP session establishment/FIB routes, or node3<->node4 reachability) were directly re-verified before proceeding to the next node.
